reason: At base the JIT fastpass bug leaks the swallowed issue's value into the result, so validating {} yields data:{a:"leaked"} and the 'a' key is present, contradicting the expected result.
At head the generated branch guards both issue concat and value assignment on presence, so an absent key produces success with no 'a' key and a present failing value is rejected.
At base marked only treats a spaces-only line as blank, so the tab-only line is swallowed and the two paragraphs merge into one instead of producing two paragraph elements.
At head the paragraph continuation lookahead treats [ \t]+\n as blank, so a tab-only line separates the text into two paragraph elements as expected.
The change only touches error-path stack decoration in Axios.request's catch handler; successful JSON response parsing is untouched, so the data property is still a parsed object at base.
The stack-decoration change does not affect response parsing, so a successful JSON request still resolves with data as a parsed object at head.
The negative-number exponent regex change does not touch boolean flag parsing; --verbose still reads true with no unknown-option error at base.
The regex change only widens accepted exponent forms for negative numbers; boolean flag handling is unaffected, so the flag reads true at head.
At base JsonTreeReader.nextInt lacks ASCII validation, so Integer.parseInt silently coerces full-width digits to 123 instead of raising a parsing error.
At head JsonTreeReader.nextInt validates the string is all-ASCII before parsing, so full-width digits raise MalformedJsonException as expected.
At base the alphanumeric-only regex splits 'test-db' into 'test' and 'db', producing 'set search_path to "test", "db"' instead of the single schema name.
At head the delimiter-blocklist regex keeps hyphens and accented characters in one schema name, so 'test-db' is quoted as a single schema.
The ByteBufferUtil.fromStream resource-leak change does not touch transformation eligibility or request options, so a center-crop transformation is still applied at base.
The change only alters buffer recycling in ByteBufferUtil; transformations remain applied unless disabled, so the crop still applies at head.
At base the union of allowed symbols and alphanumerics is recomputed on each check, so an identifier using a configured allowed symbol passes the naming rule.
At head the union is cached but refreshed whenever allowedSymbols changes, preserving the same behavior, so the identifier still passes with no violation.
Adding <cstdint> to CharData.h is a compilation-only change unrelated to image loading, so percent-encoded SVG data URIs still load and render at base.
Adding Afrikaans week/weekly locale translations does not touch datetime shifting or timezone arithmetic, so the 10-hour DST shift still yields 2025-03-09T05:30:00-05:00 at head.
The GCC 15 <cstdint> include is a compilation-only change with no effect on image loading, so percent-encoded SVG data URIs still load and draw at head.
The cookie-header parsing change is unrelated to content decoding, so decoding an empty form-urlencoded body into an all-optional type still succeeds at base.
Cookie parsing does not affect content decoders, so an empty form body still decodes to all-nil optionals without a 422 at head.
The PR only fixes spelling in comments and a test variable name; the in-memory filesystem Remove behavior is unchanged, so a non-empty directory is still rejected at base.
Spelling-only changes do not affect filesystem semantics, so Remove on a non-empty directory still returns an error and leaves the contents in place at head.
The JSON flags-as-depth fix in JsonTest is unrelated to schema comparison, so comparing schemas with two equally valid index rename candidates still completes without PHP warnings at base.
The JSON flags-as-depth fix only touches a test helper, not schema comparison, so comparing schemas with two rename candidates still completes without PHP warnings at head.
Adding Afrikaans week translations does not touch datetime shift or timezone arithmetic, so the 10-hour shift across the DST boundary still yields 2025-03-09T05:30:00-05:00 at base.

The PR changes only CircuitBreakerStateMachine predicate handling, which does not affect the semaphore rate limiter's scheduled refresh, so permits keep replenishing after the limit is lowered at base.
Circuit-breaker predicate changes do not affect rate limiter scheduling, so the refresh task keeps replenishing up to the lowered limit at head.
The no-var autofix rewrites `var a` to `let a`, which puts a in the temporal dead zone, so foo() called before the declaration throws a ReferenceError instead of printing undefined.
After the autofix converts `var count` to `let count`, the indirectly invoked printCount accesses count before initialization and throws a ReferenceError rather than printing undefined.
The logformatter_adapter change does not touch crawl scheduling or job persistence, so a SitemapSpider restarted with a persisted JOBDIR resumes remaining URLs instead of closing immediately at base.
Log-formatting changes do not affect job persistence, so the resumed crawl still requests remaining sitemap URLs and only closes after actual pages are crawled at head.

The sanitize bidi-control PR does not touch wrapping or highlighting code, and printing a double-width character at --terminal-width 1 is the known capacity-overflow panic class; the PR only lists the snip-separator variant as fixed, so the crash likely still occurs at base.
The sanitize PR does not fix the capacity-overflow path for wrapping wide characters at --terminal-width 1 with a row-filling background, so bat likely still aborts at head.
The syslog parser regex change is unrelated to out_file buffering, and the plugin creates a per-chunk symlink for each chunk key, so both aa and bb symlinks are created in a single multi-key batch.
The syslog regex PR does not touch file output symlinks, so a follow-up record for a previously-seen key still creates/updates that key's symlink at head.

Pool-name generation uses a counter, not a lock on System.getProperties(), and the ConcurrentBag virtual-thread change does not affect pool construction, so building a pool does not block on unrelated system-property access at base.
ConcurrentBag changes do not touch pool-name generation or system-property access, so concurrently starting multiple pools does not deadlock with unrelated System.getProperties() holders at head.
The SORT ACL key-check change does not affect RDB persistence, and a few-megabyte dataset is well within 32-bit Redis capabilities, so BGSAVE succeeds with rdb_last_bgsave_status:ok at base.
SORT ACL changes do not touch persistence, so the automatic background save of a growing dataset completes successfully without signal termination at head.
The CWD/globaldir change in nvim_win_set_buf does not affect number increment logic, so CTRL-A on the 50-digit number still adds exactly one, preserving all digits at base.
The cwd-context fix does not touch CTRL-X arithmetic, so decrementing the 50-digit number still preserves every digit at head.
The external-file-cache PR does not touch array concatenation binding, and DuckDB binds [1] || NULL as list concat so the result keeps INTEGER[] type holding NULL at base.
The file-cache change is unrelated to list operators, so typeof([1] || NULL) matches typeof(list_concat([1], NULL)) as a list type at head.

The ScrollBar input change does not affect RefCounted lifetime, and NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE fires during the destructor while members are still valid, so the override runs and reads its member safely at base.
ScrollBar touch handling does not touch RefCounted destruction, so releasing the last reference still runs the PREDELETE handler with valid members and no crash at head.
The DecisionTree categorical-feature error does not affect feature selection, and f_regression handles a constant column as r=0 giving F=0.0 and p=1.0 without NaN or sqrt warnings at base.
The tree criterion change is unrelated to r_regression, which clamps correlation to [-1,1] for near-constant columns, returning a finite value without RuntimeWarning at head.
The swagger-ui JS change is unrelated to Vault Agent's file sink, which honors the configured octal mode, so the token file is written with 0640 permissions at base.
The UI change does not affect Vault Agent, so a file sink mode of 0600 produces an owner-only token file at head.
At base write_usage with empty args emitted only a blank line (issue #3360), so --help for a command with no options prints no 'Usage: cli' first line.
At head write_usage writes the prefix and program name even with empty args and strips the trailing separator, so the first line reads exactly 'Usage: cli'.
The IPv6 host-parsing change does not affect response serialization, so a view returning a dict is still served as compact application/json at base.
Host/port resolution changes do not touch view dispatch or JSON serialization, so dict-returning views still get application/json with compact bodies at head.
The unhashable-generic-alias schema fix does not touch required-field validation, so constructing a model without a required field still raises a ValidationError identifying it as missing at base.
The DEPRECATED_ALIASES lookup change only affects schema generation for generic aliases, not field validation, so omitting a required field still fails with a missing-field error at head.
logging.WARN and logging.WARNING are the same numeric level (30), so replacing the constant does not change behavior; echo off still suppresses INFO SQL logging at base.
The WARN to WARNING rename is value-identical, so the engine's effective level still blocks INFO records with echo off and logs the statement with echo on at head.
At base, once attribute methods are generated, the computed alias attribute is read through the method_missing fallback without exception handling, so its access cost stays within the 20x threshold.

At head every computed-attribute read forces define_attribute_methods plus a public_instance_method lookup that raises and rescues a NameError, making the alias read far exceed 20x the real-column cost.
At base getCalledListeners iterates the callStack, which holds one WrappedListener per dispatch, so two dispatches of one listener report two entries.
At head postProcess deduplicates called listeners per event (in_array check), so two dispatches of the same listener report only one entry, not the expected two.
The shellcheck-driven COMPREPLY rewrite does not change which command is active or how custom completion hooks are invoked, so each subcommand still gets scoped suggestions at base.
The COMPREPLY assignment style and pushd guard do not affect the current-command logic passed to completion hooks, so subcommand-scoped suggestions still appear at head.
At base (qs 6.13.0) repeated keys beyond the default arrayLimit of 20 parse into a numeric-keyed object, so 25 'ids' values are not returned as an array.
The qs 6.14.0 bump fixes repeated-key arrays so ?ids=1..25 parses as an array of 25 strings in order at head.
At base get_environ_proxies takes only a url argument, so calling it with a single URL returns the proxies dict without error.
At head get_environ_proxies requires a no_proxy argument with no default, so calling it with only the URL raises a TypeError, breaking the third-party integration.
At base parse_unit_value rejects dot-leading tokens outright, so .foons falls through to a bare-word string parse and the list element is '.foons'.
At head the dot-leading token enters parse_unit_value but '.foons' fails float parsing and falls back to a string, so [.foons] | get 0 still yields '.foons'.
At base the curl handler connects a sink write function even for HEAD requests, which errors when combined with an Accept-Encoding header, so the HEAD request fails fatally.
At head no sink/write function is connected for HEAD requests, so the HEAD request with Accept-Encoding completes and returns a valid response.
At base the diff formatter mishandles the map value that is an improper list, so formatting the match failure crashes instead of producing a clean diff showing :foo vs %{bar: [1|2]}.
At head maps are converted to AST for diffing, so the match failure for %{bar: [1|2]} formats cleanly without an additional crash.
At base the css_props teardown removes the element and dynamic css-props components fail to keep the custom property, so the inner component text is not red after the toggle.
At head dynamic css-props components are compiled through build_component and the element-removing teardown is dropped, so the --prop color (red) persists before and after the toggle.
At base the guard only checks code.includes for 'new URL' and 'import.meta.url', and the match regex uses \s* so a multi-line new URL(asset, import.meta.url) is bundled as a static asset.

At head the transform filter regex /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/ uses '.' which does not match newlines, so a multi-line new URL(...) call fails the filter and is never transformed to an emitted asset.
At base no FZF_CURRENT_ITEM env var is exported, so the preview child process is launched with a clean environment and 'echo ok' runs fine for NUL-containing items.
At head FZF_CURRENT_ITEM carries the item text including NUL bytes into the child env, and Go rejects environment entries containing NUL, so the preview command fails to start.
At base switching to edge-to-edge calls setSystemUiVisibility with only LAYOUT flags, clearing the immersiveSticky hide flags, so the system bars reappear.

At head switching to edge-to-edge only calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) and returns early without clearing the immersiveSticky HIDE_NAVIGATION/FULLSCREEN flags, so the bars stay hidden.
At base ruff has no multiple-assignment-in-case check, so case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes) reports no syntax error and passes cleanly.
At head the visitor inserts the class keyword attribute name as a binding, so num_classes=num_classes is reported as a duplicate assignment even though it is valid Python.
At base the value-slice decoder assumes the destination slice is already large enough, so the second nested block indexes past the placeholder length and panics with index out of range.
At head the decoder grows the slice with reflect.Append when blocks exceed the current length, so two blocks decode into two entries without panic, overwriting the placeholder.
At base setTestNow without an explicit timezone keeps the mocked moment in America/Los_Angeles, so Carbon::now() formats in LA rather than the UTC default.
At head the mock converts the test instance to the application default timezone when none is pinned, so Carbon::now() presents the UTC representation.
At base the regex /^[\\/]{2}[^\\/]+/ rejects triple-slash, whitespace-separated, and mixed-slash leading forms, so none of the three inputs is classified as protocol-relative.
At head /^([\\/]\s*){2,}[^\\/]/ matches three leading slashes, slashes separated by tab, and a slash followed by backslash, so all three inputs are protocol-relative.
The combineOrdered/combineUnordered internal-accessor change does not affect single-input hashing, so Hashing.md5() of 'abc' still yields 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72 at base.
The getBytesInternal swap only touches hash-combining helpers and produces identical values, so the MD5 digest of 'abc' is unchanged at head.
Moving diagnostic descriptors to a dedicated class does not change generator behavior, so the annotated interface still generates a client issuing the correct GET request at base.
The diagnostics refactor is behavior-neutral, so source generation still completes and the generated client issues the expected GET request at head.
Removing trailing redundant continue statements does not change control flow, so a simple HTTP/1.1 GET still returns the fixed 200 body correctly at base.
The needless_continue cleanup preserves loop semantics, so the fresh HTTP/1.1 request still gets status 200 and the exact configured body at head.
At base the :basic format argument is dropped after the calendar conversion, so to_iso8601(holo_date, :basic) silently returns the extended '2001-01-01' instead of '20010101'.
At head the format is forwarded to to_iso8601/2 after conversion, so the basic call returns '20010101' while the default returns '2001-01-01'.
At base setEndDate updates the internal end-date state but the native DatePeriod 'end' property is not re-synchronized on PHP 8.2+, so it still reports 2024-09-30.
At head syncNativePeriod reinitializes the native DatePeriod after setEndDate, so both 'end' and getEndDate() report 2025-06-15 00:00:00.
At base there is no whitespace check, so a custom normalizer that passes a newline through lets the client send a request line with an embedded newline instead of raising.
At head headline and host construction raise RequestError when the resolved path or host contains whitespace, so the newline-containing request is refused before transmission.
The Albanian locale change does not touch English number-to-words, so 1,000,000 still converts to 'one million' and 2,000,000 to 'two million' at base.
Only the sq.yml Albanian scale word changes, so default-English conversions remain 'one million' and 'two million' at head.
The property-save crash fix does not affect component scoping, so resolving the singleton twice still returns the identical instance at base.
The non-String property filtering only changes property loading, not definition scoping, so singleton resolution still returns the same instance both times at head.
At base replaceElement appends, swaps, and removes to put ('z', 2) at index 1 while preserving order, and the duplicate-key precondition still fails for 'a'.
At head the shared _replaceNew primitive plus value exchange yields the same ('a',1),('z',2),('c',3) order, and the duplicate-key precondition still fires before any mutation.
The manual negative clamp and max(x, 0) are equivalent, so '-5MB' still parses to 0 bytes at base.
The built-in max(cast.ToInt(sizeStr), 0) preserves the clamp-to-zero behavior, so '-5MB' returns 0 bytes at head.
At base findCaseInsensitivePathRec grabs children[0] when wildChild is set, hitting a static node whose type panics as 'invalid node type', so both the mis-cased and unmatched lookups crash.
At head static children are tried via indices before the wildcard child at the end, so /PREFIX/XXX redirects to /prefix/xxx and unmatched paths return not-found without panicking.
At base a valid Numeric with nil Int reaches toBigInt which returns nil, and IsInt64 dereferences it, so Int64Value panics instead of returning zero.
At head toBigInt returns big.NewInt(0) for a nil Int, so Int64Value succeeds with zero, matching Float64Value and Value.
The renderer tab-stop change does not affect the program run loop, so calling Quit from another goroutine still makes run return promptly without error at base.
Tab-stop handling only affects terminal rendering, not shutdown signaling, so external Quit still returns from run without hanging at head.
At base the already-cancelled token's wait future is not immediately ready on the first poll, so the wrapped future is polled and its panic executes instead of returning a cancelled outcome.
At head is_cancelled() is checked before the wrapped future is ever polled, so an already-cancelled token returns None immediately and the panicking operation never starts.
The ignore-file loading change does not affect search matching, so case-insensitive search still reports every line containing the term at base.
Only unreachable ignore-file loading is skipped, which does not change case-insensitive matching, so all case variants of the term still match at head.
At base a skip_deserializing field with no custom default is initialized via Default::default(), so the omitted field holds its type's default value.
The nesting refactor is equivalent (Default::None matches container_default.is_none()), so the skipped field still receives Default::default() when the input omits it at head.
